figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Features of the pV2A-T plasmid described by Hoefgen et al. (2018) and of the two plasmids, pHYX137 and pHYX138, adapted for S. cerevisiae expression, described 
in this study. Complete maps are shown in Supplementary File 2.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Confocal microscopy of the yeast strain BJNBC-003 expressing Venus-NLS and mScarlet-I fluorescent proteins and stained with DAPI to detect DNA. A-D, Bar 
= 50 μm. E-H, from left to right, bright-field image showing the yeast cells, red fluorescence corresponding to mScarlet-I, yellow fluorescence corresponding to Venus 
and, blue fluorescence corresponding to DAPI. The mScarlet-I signal is distributed throughout the cell whereas the Venus signal is co-localized with DNA in the 
nucleus. Bar = 5 μm.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. General overview of the biosynthetic gene cluster BGC16 (A) and its conservation and microsynteny in genome-sequenced Colletotrichum spp. (B). The BGC is actually 
composed of two BGCs side-by-side or intertwined, one for biosynthesis of Colletochlorins and the other for biosynthesis of Higginsianins. The Higginsianin genes (dpch) were 
characterized by Tsukada et al. (2020). The gene CH63R_05474 is a pseudogene whereas the gene CH63R_05472 encodes a predicted transcription factor. When present, 
regions composed of repeated transposable elements are shown as double-headed arrows together with their length. Vertical red bars denote contig ends. Fungal BGCs are often 
misassembled during genome sequencing and split over several contigs due to difficult-to-assemble long stretches of repeats. The intensity of grey/black shading represents the 
percentage of amino acid identity.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. Conservation and microsynteny of the Colletochlorin (ctc) biosynthetic genes cluster in fungi. In Colletotrichum higginsianum IMI 349063A, this BGC was initially 
predicted to be a single BGC16 but actually comprises the dpch (Higginsianins) and ctc BGCs located side-by-side. Genes are color-coded according to their putative or 
experimentally-confirmed functions. The intensity of grey/black shading represents the percentage of amino acid identity. Experimentally-verified BGCs are shown with one of 
their molecular products. Hy, Hypocreaceae; is, incertæ sedis; Mg, Magnaporthaceae; St, Stachybotryaceae.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Monitoring the production of Colletochlorin biosynthetic intermediates using HPLC-PDA-ELSD-MS. (A) ELSD chromatogram of crude extracts of strains BJNBC-001 
(empty vector) and BJNBC-008 (ctc1 to ctc4 genes expressed from a polycistron) and the Orsellinic acid standard. Only Orsellinic acid could be detected among the known 
intermediates of the Colletochlorin family. (B) UV spectra of the differential peak identified in BJNBC-008 (asterisk) and of the Orsellinic acid standard.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. Proposed biosynthetic pathways of the Colletochlorins. (A) Domain structure of CTC1 and CTC3 proteins. (B) Hypothetical scenario 1 where the CTC4 
prenyltransferase accepts only DMAPP (dimethylallylpyrophosphate) as isoprene donor. (C) Hypothetical scenario 2 where the CTC4 prenyltransferase accepts both 
DMAPP and GPP (geranylpyrophosphate) as isoprene donors. Domains: ACP, acyl-carrier protein; AT, acyl transferase; KS, ketosynthase; PT, product template; SAT, 
starter-unit acyltransferase; TE, thioesterase; A, adenylation; PCP, peptidyl-carrier protein; R, reduction.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 7. Immunodetection of the CTC proteins and VenusN. (A) Immunoblot of whole-cell protein extracts from the strains BJNBC-001 (empty vector) and BJNBC-008 (ctc 
genes) at t0 (optical density of 0.4; repressive medium replaced by inductive medium) and t24 after induction. The proteins were detected with an anti-2A antibody. Note that 
VenusN is present also in the empty vector. Equal loading was assessed using TGX Stain-Free gels. (B) Schematic representation of the expected proteins with their size.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 8. Combined extracted ion chromatograms (EIC) of the culture supernatant of the strain BJNBC-015 expressing all four ctc genes in a polycistron and an additional copy 
of ctc4 (prenyltransferase) with its own promoter. EIC of standards of the different biosynthetic intermediates in the Colletochlorin pathway are also represented.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 9
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 9. LC-MS/MS fragmentation pattern of, A, a Colletochlorin B standard and, B, a molecule annotated as Colletorin B from the BJNBC-015 strain. Detailed 
fragmentation patterns are presented in Supplementary File 5.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 10
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 10. Relative abundance of Colletochlorins and their biosynthetic intermediates by LC-QToF. Crude extracts of the culture supernatants and cell pellets were analysed for S. 
cerevisiae cultures whereas crude extracts of the mixed supernatant and mycelia was analysed for the organism of origin of the ctc BGC, C. higginsianum (Ch63A). Extracts 
from an empty-vector strain (no biosynthetic genes) were included as controls for the yeast. The values from two independent experiments are presented and are expressed as 
relative abundance per mg of crude extract, resuspended in methanol.
